newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD - Pullback forecast for HK's Hang Seng.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Pullback forecast for HK's Hang Seng.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks appear to be in the midst of a much-needed pullback, and brokers and analysts say a further consolidation -- as much as 200 points -- in the coming week would be positive.

"The Hong Kong market climbed to record highs in a short time and is quite overbought. It is also more volatile at this level and prone to profit-taking," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities Hong Kong Ltd.

The Hang Seng Index closed down 85.19 points at 12,388.38 on Friday. Over the four-day week, the index eased a total of 121.64 points or one percent. Turnover remained robust with daily turnover averaging HK$6.84 billion.
Last Monday was a holiday in Hong Kong.
During the week the index fell three times to test the 12,430-point level, then rebounded confirming chartists' support levels.

Brokers said the market's volatility was due to conflicting goals of genuine profit-taking at these record levels, and futures market arbitrageurs hoping to see the cash market remain at higher levels in advance of the expiry of the October futures contract on October 30.
"I think there are a lot of long positions (in October futures) out there," said a broker at a Japanese house.
Analysts' longer term views on the market remain bullish.

"Until something fundamental changes, investors will keep buying on dips. We are confident on the medium term outlook for the market," said Au-Young. "The market is fairly valued at this level (12,400). At the same time I expect the market to go much higher in 1997."
However, short-term technical indicators were looking less positive, analysts said.

"We still need to see confirmation from the relative strength indicator, but the current trend points to as much as a 200-point correction in the week ahead," said Alan Shum, research manager at New Century Securities Ltd. "The index could test the 12,100-200 level."
Market leaders HSBC and Hang Seng Bank are likely to consolidate in line with the market, analysts said.
Alex Wong, technical analyst at Dharmala Securities Ltd, however, is still bullish on HSBC Holdings.
"Since this rally began, each correction in HSBC has been very shallow, so we could see a big correction but (that would be) followed by a surge to HK$180 in late 1996," he said.
